cases.title: 'Do the rest' before any demo is the ask: the one demo runs, the rest handed back in one sentence, no later offer

rubric.reason: In Turn 3 the learner asked 'Can you hold the rest for me?' before any demo, and the mentor ran the one key_types_demo on the 1 s pair. It said what changed and that 'Edit > Undo reverses it', then handed back 'The 1.4 s and 1.8 s pairs are yours. Say done when you've held them.' It did not repeat the how-to or offer to do the others.

Turn 3 describes one change in plain words with real names ('I held one pair for you: the key on Blink's Opacity at 1 s'), matching the demo result (1–1.4 s, out_type hold, values 100 to 0). It gives the generic 'Edit > Undo' rather than an undo label, uses no field names, and makes no offer to do the rest.

Each turn is short and ends with something for the learner. Turn 1 ends on the snap question, and Turn 2 gives one idea plus the how-to and ends 'Hold Blink's three pairs and say done.' Turn 3 is the demo with a one-sentence handback, and Turn 4 is 'That passes' with what was held, ending on the constant-speed question.

Turn 3: asked to 'hold the rest' before any demo, the mentor ran one key_types_demo on the 1 s pair, said what changed and that Edit > Undo reverses it, then handed back 'The pairs starting at 1.4 s and 1.8 s are yours to hold. Say done when you've finished.' It did not repeat the how-to or offer to do more.

Turn 3: one change, described in plain words with real names ('I held Blink's Opacity key at 1 s, so Blink stays fully showing until 1.4 s and then snaps away'), matching the demo result (out_type hold, 1 to 1.4 s); it names Edit > Undo, uses no field names and makes no offer to do the rest.

Each turn is short and ends on a hand-off: Turn 2 is the idea plus one task ending 'Hold Blink's three pairs and say done', Turn 3 is the demo turn ending with the hand-back, and Turn 4 is 'That passes' with what they held, ending on the linear question; no turn is a lecture.

In Turn 3, after 'Can you hold the rest for me?' and before any demo, the mentor ran one key_types_demo on the 1 s pair, said what changed in plain words, said 'Edit > Undo reverses it', and handed back with 'The 1.4 s and 1.8 s pairs are yours. Say done when they're held.' It did not repeat the how-to or offer to do the others.

Turn 3 describes one change ('Blink's Opacity key at 1 s is now a hold') in plain words with real names and times backed by the demo result. It says 'Edit > Undo reverses it', names no undo label or field names, and hands the 1.4 s and 1.8 s pairs back without offering to do them.

The Turn 4 pass turn adds a recap before the linear question: 'The 1 s pair is the one I held for you, and you held the 1.4 s and 1.8 s pairs yourself. Blink now snaps back on at 1.8 s and off again at 2.2 s, with no fade in between.' That goes beyond 'That passes' plus one clause on what was held.
